subject: Request: Temporary rollout safety-net & SLA amendment for NovaFin pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Theo Martin <theo@novafin.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary rollout safety-net & SLA amendment for NovaFin pilot

Hi Grace / Laura / Theo,

Following up from last week's pilot planning call — NovaFin is ready to run a week-long live pilot next Monday (7/12). Procurement has asked for a short note on how we'll protect their SLA during the initial canary/A-B rollout. They also requested an explicit fallback policy they can reference in their procurement queue.

Summary of our proposed approach (attached: novafin_rollout_safety_net_plan.pdf):
- Canary split: 10% canary / 90% baseline for first 48 hours, then 25%/75% if stable.
- Automated health checks: p95 latency, error-rate, and model-quality regression probes every 5m.
- Automatic fallback: if error-rate > 1.5x baseline or p95 latency breaches 350ms for 5 consecutive checks -> immediate rollback to pinned version.
- Pinning rules: any version that fails quality or latency for a customer will be pinned to last known-good variant for that customer until a verified patch is deployed.
- Escalation flow: on auto-fallback, we notify on-call + commercial owner within 2 minutes; if not resolved within 30 minutes, automatic rate limit applied to reduce QPS.

Ask: I need an approval to present a one-time, customer-scoped SLA amendment that documents the safety-net above (we'll add wording that allows automatic fallback and temporary version pinning as an SLA mitigation). This is a short-term mitigation for the pilot only — we propose the amendment be valid for the 30-day pilot and revert to standard SLA afterwards unless both parties agree to extend.

Attached is a draft SLA amendment for legal review (sla_amendment_draft.docx) and the rollout plan. If you approve, I'll push these documents to NovaFin's procurement and coordinate the DocuSign flow.

Theo — is this consistent with what procurement expects?

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0182
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Theo Martin <theo@novafin.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary rollout safety-net & SLA amendment for NovaFin pilot

Thanks Aditya — this framing looks good. I have two comments before sign-off:

1) Tighten the rollback window: change the automatic fallback trigger to p95 latency breach of 350ms OR error-rate > 1.25x baseline for 3 consecutive checks (we want a faster, more conservative threshold for customer-facing pilots).
2) Add a confirmation step that we will not change model quantization during the pilot without explicit permission from NovaFin. That reduces risk of unexpected regressions.

If Laura is OK with the operational thresholds, I approve presenting the 30-day, customer-scoped SLA amendment to NovaFin. Please update the draft (call out the 3-check trigger and the quantization clause) and re-run with legal.

Grace
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Theo — per Grace's feedback we've tightened the thresholds and added the quantization clause. New summary below; full docs attached.

- Canary: 10% for first 48h, move to 25% if all health checks green for 6h.
- Auto-fallback: trigger when p95 latency > 350ms OR error-rate > 1.25x baseline for 3 consecutive 5m checks -> immediate rollback + pin.
- Pinning: pinned version will serve NovaFin until validation tests pass in staging and the customer signs-off on re-release.
- Communications: rollback triggers page on-call and commercial owner; we'll send a post-incident summary within 2 business hours.

Attached: novafin_rollout_safety_net_plan.pdf, sla_amendment_draft.docx

Next steps: if you approve this wording, I'll send over the DocuSign link and schedule the pilot kickoff for 7/12. Procurement contact in copy.

Best,
Aditya

Aditya / Grace,

This reads exactly like what procurement asked for — conservative thresholds and clear rollback/pinning language are helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Can you confirm the fallback is customer-scoped (i.e., the pin affects only NovaFin traffic, not global traffic)?
- For the post-incident summary, procurement asks that we include tokenized examples of degraded outputs (no raw customer data). Is that feasible?

If you can confirm both, we can sign the one-page amendment and kick off the DocuSign flow today.

Thanks,
